name: TOM
aliases: Testosterone in Older Men with Mobility Limitations
question: In older men with low testosterone and mobility limitation, how do testosterone gel and placebo compare for strength and cardiovascular adverse events?

design.population: Community-dwelling men aged at least 65 years with mobility difficulty, Short Physical Performance Battery scores of 4–9, and total testosterone 100–350 ng/dL or free testosterone below 50 pg/mL.
design.locator: Primary full text, Methods: Study Design, Study Participants; Results: Enrollment; Table 1

verdictNote: Leg-press strength improved, but excess cardiovascular-related events prompted early termination.
takeaway: In mobility-limited older men with low testosterone, daily 1% testosterone gel improved leg-press strength versus placebo gel, but cardiovascular-related adverse events occurred in 23/106 versus 5/103 men and the trial stopped early.

reports.label: Initial safety and efficacy report
reports.citation: Basaria S, Coviello AD, Travison TG, et al. "Adverse Events Associated with Testosterone Administration." *N Engl J Med.* 2010;363(2):109-122. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1000485
reports.followUp: Planned 24-week treatment and 3-month observation; stopped before target enrollment
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods: Procedures; Results: Enrollment; Discussion

results.measure: Change in maximal voluntary leg-press force; unadjusted mean difference in change, newtons
results.note: Prespecified efficacy endpoint; efficacy assessments were available for a subset after early termination.
results.locator: Full text, Methods: Procedures and Statistical Analysis; Table 5, leg-press strength

results.measure: Men with at least one cardiovascular-related event; unadjusted odds ratio
results.note: Broad safety-board category assembled after review; cardiovascular events were not a prespecified endpoint.
results.locator: Full text, Methods: Safety Monitoring; Results: Adverse Events; Table 3; Table 4, unadjusted odds ratio

results.measure: Change in chest-press force; unadjusted mean difference in change, newtons
results.note: Efficacy assessment subset after early termination.

harms.label: MedDRA cardiac disorders
harms.locator: Full text, Results: Adverse Events; Table 3
harms.note: Men with at least one cardiac event under the original MedDRA classification.

harms.label: Atherosclerosis-related events
harms.locator: Full text, Methods: Safety Monitoring; Results: Adverse Events; Table 3
harms.note: Safety-board category included myocardial infarction, sudden death, revascularization, and stroke.

delivery.label: Gel regimen and titration
delivery.value: Testim 1% gel, 10 g (100 mg testosterone) daily for 6 months; after 2 weeks, titrate to 5 g daily if the average of two testosterone measurements exceeded 1000 ng/dL or to 15 g daily if the average was below 500 ng/dL.

delivery.label: Enrollment and efficacy analysis
delivery.value: 209/252 planned men randomized; 129 completed 6 months; 176 had at least one postrandomization efficacy assessment; the safety board recommended stopping enrollment and treatment on 2009-12-31.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results: Enrollment of Subjects and Discontinuation of the Study

delivery.label: Delivered doses and adherence
delivery.value: At titration, 29 received 5 g, 61 received 10 g, and 16 received 15 g daily; tube-count adherence exceeded 90% in both groups.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results: Testosterone Dose and Adherence

reports.label: Patient-important physical function
reports.citation: Travison TG, Basaria S, Storer TW, et al. "Clinical Meaningfulness of the Changes in Muscle Performance and Physical Function Associated With Testosterone Administration in Older Men With Mobility Limitation." *J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci.* 2011;66(10):1090-1099. doi:10.1093/gerona/glr100
reports.followUp: 6-month treatment; 165 men with follow-up efficacy measures

results.measure: Proportion exceeding minimally important difference in stair-climbing power
results.note: Secondary analysis; arm-specific denominators are absent from the abstract.
